allNewsData.title: Everything ChatGPT at SV Code Campfire
allNewsData.contentData:
On Saturday, we had four great ChatGPT sessions. As promised, Glenn Block did some great examples of using ChatGPT for the first time in his session. Jerry Nixon talked about ChatGPT in higher education in his, and then Carson Lam did a pretty technically deep discussion around what's inside if you wanted to built your own ChatGPT. Finally, Junling Hu did a great job of introducing what the science is behind ChatGPT and did an excellent job of defining what a lot of the terms people throw out there are and what they mean.
 
Click on this link to see the full PlayList including the Q&As after each session. The Q&A after the second talk between was really good IMHO.
 
 
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL7hKLAqgemJCCkbYd8WxDmiHOU0JWikNY
 
 
Sessions below that include links to the individual videos
 

YouTube Link 		ChatGPT, It Will Blow Your Mind Glenn Block

YouTube Link 		Generative AI and Computer Science in Higher Education Jerry Nixon

YouTube Link 		Will ChatGPT Do X? Build Your Own Mini-ChatGPT and Then Decide for Yourself Carson Lam

YouTube Link 		The Science Behind ChatGPT Junling Hu
 
 
See you next time!
 
Best Regards,
Peter Kellner, Organizer, Silicon Valley Code Camp and SV Campfire

allNewsData.description: Click through to learn everything you need to know as a registered attendee of Silicon Valley Code Camp 2019. This includes our full schedule Saturday and Sunday as well as other important details like parking.
allNewsData.title: The Goods! (Everything)
allNewsData.contentData:
Most important. BRING YOUR ID. PayPal security will check it and match to your SV Code Camp Badge at the door, and without that, you cannot get in. Our records show that you are registered for at least one day of Code Camp.
 
Silicon Valley Code Camp hosted by PayPal, starts this Saturday! Badge pickup starts at 8:15AM. After that join us for  coffee, networking with friends, and time with our sponsors. Our first session is 9:30AM.
 
Douglas Crockford will again be kicking off this year talking about the History of JSON (something he invented). Also in the first time slot, Eve Porcello will be talking about React being your friend. If you want to hear about why you keep getting those cookie warning on your web sites (and why we don't need one for Silicon Valley Code Camp), learn about GDPR with Claudia Galvan.
 
One of the big surprises this year is how popular career type talks are. Soham Mehta is talking about defying ageism at 1PM with a panel of FAANG Engineering managers at 2:15PM (and find out what FAANG is if you did not know already).  Side note: Soham, Founder of InterviewKickstart will happily review your resume if you bring it by their sponsor table.
 
Parking is free for all Code Camp attendees and can be found all around PayPal Town Hall.  Basically, it's the employee parking for thousands and it's a weekend so it is plentiful for us.
 
We will have printed copies of the schedule, but you can help us out by printing and bringing the following PDF files, they contain the session schedules for both Saturday & Sunday. Or if you love trees, skip the printing and use our new mobile app (http://svcc.mobi). The new mobile app lets you view sessions by time, room and alphabetically.

allNewsData.title: Call for Speakers SVCC 2017
allNewsData.contentData:
We are excited to announce our Call for Speakers. PayPal is hosting our SV Code Camp at PayPal Town Hall on Saturday and Sunday October 7th and 8th in San Jose.  It’s an awesome facility and we are honored to be there.  Our format this year will be different than the past 11 years of Code Camps. 

Town Hall’s capacity limits us to 800 attendees and since there are 12 speaking rooms, we will have less sessions.  Sessions will be 45 minutes this year with 7 slots on Saturday and 6 on Sunday.
Get your proposals in ASAP.  We will approve some sessions immediately and others later. We plan on opening registration within a week or two so don’t delay in getting your sessions proposals in.

We still are searching for great sponsors and of course, sponsorship does give you a leg up in getting your session approved.  If your company is interested in sponsoring, please let us know by sending email to sponsorship@siliconvalley-codecamp.com
 
Call for Speakers Link: /Session/Submit

Looking forward to a great year 12!

allNewsData.contentData:
Hi SV Code Camper,

I’m excited to announce that PayPal will host our 12th Silicon Valley Code Camp on October 7-8, 2017 at the PayPal Town Hall in San Jose. With this location we can significantly increase our live-streaming content, allowing people around the world to participate.
 
However, because this is an indoor venue, we will have challenges to overcome. For starters, attendance will be limited to 800 people and 90 sessions, so we will have to find ways to accurately predict attendance, which might include:
  • A nominal lunch fee
  • More focused sessions
That said, I’m 100% confident that with our awesome crew of speakers, volunteers and sponsors, we will make this the best code camp yet. Stay tuned for more details.
Regards,
Peter Kellner

allNewsData.title: 2016 Kids Call For Speakers
allNewsData.contentData:
We still need several more SVCC Kids Sunday instructors.  If you love teaching kids and want to give one or more 75 minute sessions, please head over to our session submission URL and make sure to check “Kid Session” when you submit your proposal.

Silicon Valley Code Camp for Kids (/kids) is an event focused on promoting programming, robotics and engineering to kids in a fun and hands-on way. Our mission is to bring together the best and brightest of Silicon Valley tech community and the kids, the next generation best and brightest. The event is targeted at kids from 5-18 yrs old kids who would like to get their first exposure to technology, or hone their skills with specialized workshops.

This email is requesting educators to submit workshops on a topic of their interest. A workshop is 75 minutes long and you can submit multi-part workshops.

What are some of the topics that would be relevant?

  • Build some games in your browser?
  • Do you like to tinker with Tynker, Scratch, Blockly, Greenfoot or any other such technology?
  • Have you been giving workshops on LEGO, Arduino, RaspberryPi, Intel Galileo, or any other fancy boards?
  • Would you like to show a real practical use case of Internet of Things to kids using simple software and hardware?
  • How about some Java, JavaScript, Scala, HTML5, CSS, Python, Ruby?
  • Building simple mobile applications using Android or iOS?
  • Paper circuits?

And of course, feel free to submit any topics that would be relevant.

Looking forward to your submissions.

Thanks
Arun Gupta,
Kids Director SVCC Kids Sunday

PS: We are recruiting SVCC Kids Sunday sponsors (local schools, companies, etc.).  Please reply to this email if you know anyone, or are interested in the exposure associated with sponsorship.

allNewsData.title: Announcing SV Code Camp 11, First Email
allNewsData.contentData:
Hi Past SV Code Camp Past Attendees,
 
Come to our 11th annual free* Silicon Valley Code Camp happening October 1-2, 2016.  Join our expected 2500+ attendees who are coming to learn what is the latest and greatest technologies from our awesome speakers and sponsors. Last year our 10th  Silicon Valley Code Camp brought multiple firsts.  The ones we are most proud of are:
  • First time we live streamed our main theatre all day Saturday (and published to YouTube)
  • First time we made the KTVU FOX 2 10PM Saturday News (45 second segment)
  • First time we made a big splash in the San Jose Mercury News
  • First time we brought in a professional photographer to memorialize our event
As always, we expect about 200 content filled sessions.  We already have four of our top speakers lined up with many more to come.
  • Douglas Crockford will be talking about the new web
  • Gayle Laakmann McDowell will be talking about careers
  • Ron Lichty and Greg Geracie will be talking about agile**
For this years Code Camp  (October 1-2, 2016) we plan on having at least one more first.  We are introducing a new Automotive Software track to recognize all the innovations that are coming to cars and how we as software and IoT people can get better involved. 
 
As always, space is limited so register now!  We are all looking forward to another great year.  Stay tuned.
 
Peter Kellner
http://peterkellner.net
Organizer
http://www.siliconvalley-codecamp.com (10/1-2/2016) and https://codestarssummit-static.github.io/codestarssummit-static/ (9/29-30/2016)
 
*As always, we count on our awesome group of sponsors to foot the bill.  If you know of any company that can help us out, please send them to our sponsorship page or have them contact us at sponsorship@siliconvalley-codecamp.com and we will get back to them with how then can help.
 
 
**Silicon Valley Code Camp encourages you to participate in the fifth annual Study of Product Team Performance. The study authors Greg Geracie and Ron Lichty have presented their findings at Code Camp for each of the past four years.

allNewsData.title: The SV Code Camp Goods!  (Everything You Need To Know)
allNewsData.contentData:
Silicon Valley Code Camp is Saturday! We are proud to continue the code camp tradtion of by developers for developers for our 10th year!  Badge Pickup starts at 8:15AM (you must be pre-registered), The president of Evergreen Valley College (Henry Yong) will welcome us with a few words to our new home at 9:15AM and then our first session is 9:45AM.
 
Feel free to enjoy coffee in the morning and visit with our sponsors right at registration. Our sponsors include Microsoft, IBM Bluemix, Samsung, Twilio, Applovin, AT&T, Bigcommerce, Couchbase, Google, Grapecity, Hurricane Electric, NewRelic, Braintree-PayPal, Raygun and Yodlee ( keep your fingers crossed for clear skies).
 
Parking is free for all Code Camp attendees but is a little tricky. There are two entrances to the college  parking lots (addresses for google maps):
  1. 3095 Yerba Buena Rd,  San Jose CA
  2. Paseo De Arboles, San Jose CA
You can enter in either one and park for free in the student spaces.
 
We will have printed copies of the schedule, but you can help us out by printing and bringing the following PDF files, they contain the session schedules for both Saturday & Sunday.  We also have a mobile app (http://svcc.mobi) that works on most iphones, androids and windows 8 phones you can use to view both your sessions as well as all sessions.

Handout_Sat_2015_Letter.pdf
Handout_Sat_2015_Extra.pdf
Handout_Sun_2015_Letter.pdf
 
Track sessions and information can be found on the web at Tracks
 
All the same information is available on the full web site at www.siliconvalley-codecamp.com and is posted on our RSS feed and shiny new news page.  Please remember to provide feedback after each session by visiting the Sessions Page on the web site and choosing Session Evaluation on the right of each session description.  Also, under the About-My Evals you can easily do all session evals from one place for all your sessions.
 
See you Very Soon!
 
Peter Kellner
Silicon Valley Code Camp Coordinator
www.siliconvalley-codecamp.com
http://peterkellner.net
 
PS: Don't forget we have a Sunday raffle at lunch time with valuable prizes being awarded often including tablets, phone and free conference passes.

allNewsData.description: If you have volunteered to help out at SV Code Camp, first, thank you!  We really appreciate and know how important you are.  Second, you should have gotten an email but if not, here are the details.  Read on...
allNewsData.title: Volunteer Instructions
allNewsData.contentData:
Hi SVCC Volunteers,
 
First and foremost, thank you for volunteering for Silicon Valley Code Camp.  SV Code Camp would not be possible without you.
 
Please don't forget, we are at Evergreen Valley College this year (NOT Foothill). Here’s the address:
 
3095 Yerba Buena Rd
San Jose, CA
 
For Friday Volunteers:
 
Please arrive at 12 noon on Friday and meet us at the EOPS. This is across from the Admissions and Records Office and across the walkway from Sequoia Hall. We need help with shirt sorting, making attendee handouts and setting up the prep rooms. If you ever felt like saying "stuff it" to someone now is your big chance because we all really do need to "stuff it," sort it and pack it. We should be done by 6pm and ready to kick back.  If you have to leave a little early that's OK.
 
There are two entrances to the college. The closest parking lots are off Yerba Buena Road on the south side of the campus; park in student parking places. Parking is $3, bring dollar bills or quarters. Parking tickets cost about $45 and Evergreen does ticket so pay the $3 instead.
 
Saturday/Sunday Volunteers:  

Important: come to the registration area 10 minutes before the start of your job assignment. Registration will be located alongside Acacia. Job assignments are here /VolunteerForJob.aspx. Please remember what you volunteered for!  We can look it up, but it's faster if you remember.
 

Remember as a volunteer you are invited to attend the speaker and volunteer appreciation dinner on Saturday night!
 
 
-Tammy

allNewsData.title: Deciphering Room Numbers With Joy Tani at Evergreen Valley College
allNewsData.contentData:
Joy has joined the staff of Silicon Valley Code Camp this year to help with all the preparation necessary to move an event of thousands of people (that's us) to a new location (that's Evergreen Valley College).  It's amazing the number of things we have to track and having Joy around to help has been amazing. From ordering tents and dumpsters, to pricing T-shirts,  to making sure we have enough food at the Saturday speakers and volunteers BBQ, there is seemingly an unlimited number of tasks.  Joy's experience as an engineering manager at Sun and program manager at TiVo helps her to understand how we think and make sure we don't screw up too badly.

In this short video, Joy seems to have decoded one of the buildings room number systems.  Let's see if she got it right when we actually use the rooms in this building for SV Code Camp next week.  I'm sure you'll meet Joy sometime over the SV Code Camp weekend proudly wearing her SV Code Camp yellow staff polo shirt.

allNewsData.contentData:
Hi SV Code Campers,
 
Our code camp schedule of 188 sessions is live!  It's important that you pick your sessions as soon as possible so we can be sure to put the most popular sessions in the largest rooms.  You now have multiple ways to choose the sessions you plan on attending.

We also have a 10 minute video that goes through in detail the best way to pick sessions and all the options.

Finally, to see your personal schedule (as well as print it), the very popular Session Overview is back.  From this screen, you can see and print all the sessions you have selected.  You can see examples of all these pages below.  As always, thanks for your support of code camp and we look forward to seeing you all in a 11 days!

allNewsData.description: We need about 250 volunteers to make SVCC run smoothly. All we ask is 2 hours and for that, you get a TShirt, Ticket to our great BBQ, a Discount on Code Stars Summit and the admiration of us and all your friends.
allNewsData.title: Looking for Volunteers, Big Rewards!!!
allNewsData.contentData:
Hi SV Code Campers,
 
Silicon Valley Code Camp needs your help.  With the big move to Evergreen Valley College and all the changes, we need more helping hands to make things run smoothly then ever.  Volunteering has so many benefits, the chance to meet and work with others like you, that feeling of goodness knowing you are contributing to our technology event, plus you're invited to attend the speaker and volunteer appreciation dinner on Saturday, you'll get a cool T-shirt, and a big discount to Code Stars Summit Workshops*.  All this for just a couple hours of your time.

Our procedure this year for volunteering is the same as the past two years.  If you want to volunteer, you need to update your registration/profile page and let us know you are interested in volunteering.  Then, after that, simply go to our "Select a Job" page and pick what suits your schedule and interest.
 
Check out this 5 minute video if you want an easy step by step on how to sign up to volunteer.
 
This registration page requires you to check the box at the bottom to volunteer, as well as put a contact mobile phone number that we can reach you on at the event itself.  Then, after you have updated your registration, go to this page: Volunteer For Job and pick the job(s) you are interested in doing.
 
Most of the jobs are 1 hour with a 15 minute overlap to train the next volunteer. A few jobs are longer 1.5 hours. We'd really appreciate volunteers who can handle 2 slots (back-to-back on Registration, which would effectively be about 2 hours).
 
Best Regards,
Peter Kellner (SVCC and Code Stars Summit Organizer)
http://peterkellner.net
http://www.siliconvalley-codecamp.com
 
PS: Hoping to send out final schedule for all SV Code Camp Sessions tomorrow!
 
* Signup for two 2 hour shifts and get a 30% Discount for any Available Code Stars Summit Workshop (first 10 volunteers only)
